name: Málaga
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Málaga: Costa del Sol property ownership, asset tracing, tech-sector due diligence and dispute support.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters connected to Málaga and the Costa del Sol: ownership research behind residential and luxury property, asset tracing for enforcement, due diligence on technology and tourism businesses, and support to counsel in Málaga proceedings. Scoped from Nashville with qualified Spanish professionals.
intro: Málaga is the capital of its province in Andalusia and Spain's sixth-largest city, with about 586,000 residents in 2024 and a metropolitan area of around 1.1 million. It is the gateway to the Costa del Sol: Málaga Airport handled about 24.9 million passengers in 2024, most of them international, and the city's tourism office counted about 14.5 million tourists and 22 million hotel nights. Alongside tourism, the city has built a technology sector around Málaga TechPark, which reported 715 companies in 2024 and turnover of about 3.46 billion euros in 2023, and international firms including Google and Vodafone have opened centres in the city. Provincial GDP grew about 2.8 percent in 2024.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Málaga largely because of the Costa del Sol property market and the international population it attracts. Residential and luxury property in Málaga, Marbella and neighbouring towns is frequently held by foreign buyers through Spanish and offshore companies, and the coast has a long history of organised crime and money laundering cases involving real estate, from Operation White Whale in Marbella in 2005 to a 2026 operation that froze 95 properties. Typical triggers include asset tracing against debtors who have moved wealth into coastal property, due diligence on developers and tourism operators, background checks on partners in the city's technology sector, and support to counsel in commercial and insolvency disputes.

matters.title: Costa del Sol property ownership
matters.text: Research into who stands behind residential and luxury property in Málaga, Marbella and the wider Costa del Sol, combining Property Registry and Mercantile Registry information obtained lawfully with corporate, court and media sources to map nominee, holding company and offshore structures.

matters.title: Asset tracing for enforcement
matters.text: Identification of property, companies, vessels and business interests on the Costa del Sol connected to a judgment or award debtor, often a foreign national who has relocated assets to Spain, so Spanish counsel can assess precautionary attachment, recognition and enforcement before Málaga courts.

matters.title: Developer and contractor due diligence
matters.text: Ownership, litigation, insolvency and reputational research on developers, builders and their financing parties in Málaga province, with attention to planning irregularities, related-party structures and links to previous failed projects, supporting lenders, buyers and joint venture partners.

matters.title: Technology sector partner checks
matters.text: Background research on start-ups, founders and investors in Málaga TechPark and the city's technology cluster, covering corporate history, related companies, litigation and adverse media, to support investments, acquisitions and partnerships with Málaga-based technology businesses. Findings are documented with sources.

matters.title: Tourism and hospitality counterparties
matters.text: Due diligence on hotel operators, tourist rental managers, marinas, golf and leisure businesses and their principals on the Costa del Sol, including ownership, licensing disputes reported publicly, adverse media and links to individuals named in financial crime investigations.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Málaga
local_context.text: Málaga is the seat of a Provincial Court (Audiencia Provincial) and of first-instance, commercial and criminal courts for the judicial district, under the national court structure described for Spain generally. Commercial courts in Málaga hear insolvency and company law matters, which frequently involve property developers and tourism businesses. Large organised crime and laundering cases on the coast are investigated by local investigating courts, sometimes alongside national bodies. Counsel should confirm the competent court for each matter.

local_context.title: Registries in Málaga province
local_context.text: Company information comes from the Mercantile Registry for Málaga and the national BORME gazette, and property information from the Property Registry offices covering each part of the province, available as notas simples showing ownership and charges. Because Costa del Sol property is often held through companies, ownership research commonly combines both registries with foreign corporate records. Access to the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership is limited to authorities, obliged entities and those showing a legitimate interest.

local_context.title: Laundering and real estate history
local_context.text: The Costa del Sol has been the focus of major laundering and corruption investigations. Operation White Whale, begun in 2003 with a main crackdown in Marbella in March 2005, recovered an estimated 250 million euros, and a related 2006 bribery inquiry led to arrests of the mayor and councillors and a caretaker administration appointed by the Junta de Andalucía. A 2026 operation with Europol froze 95 properties and shut down more than 100 companies used to invest drug proceeds in housing.

local_context.title: Regional government and investment bodies
local_context.text: Andalusia's regional government, the Junta de Andalucía, has competences in urban planning, tourism and economic development that bear on property and hospitality matters in Málaga, while the city council promotes investment through its Open for Business office and supports the technology cluster. Planning and licensing records relevant to a site or business are held by municipal and regional authorities and are generally obtained through formal requests or counsel.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Málaga, TDSC first identifies the objective and forum: enforcement against Costa del Sol assets, an insolvency or company dispute in the Málaga commercial courts, a property or development transaction, or an investment in a technology or tourism business. Ownership research combines Mercantile and Property Registry information obtained lawfully with foreign corporate records, court decisions and Spanish and English-language media. Personal data is handled under the GDPR and Spain's Organic Law 3/2018. Registry certificates and court steps are handled through Spanish counsel, and any surveillance, interviews or field inquiries are coordinated with private detectives holding the qualification required under Spanish private security law. TDSC has no office in Málaga.

faqs.q: Can TDSC find out who owns a villa in Marbella or Málaga?
faqs.a: TDSC can research registered ownership and charges through Property Registry information obtained lawfully, then trace any owning company through the Mercantile Registry and foreign corporate records. Where a chain ends in an offshore entity or nominee, TDSC uses court records, media and other lawful sources and states clearly where ultimate ownership cannot be confirmed.

faqs.q: Does TDSC trace assets of foreign debtors living on the Costa del Sol?
faqs.a: Yes. Many enforcement matters involve debtors from other countries who hold Spanish property, companies, vehicles or boats on the coast. TDSC identifies likely assets from lawful sources and documents the evidence so Spanish counsel can assess precautionary measures, recognition of the foreign judgment or award and enforcement before the Málaga courts.

faqs.q: Can TDSC check a Costa del Sol developer before we invest?
faqs.a: Yes. TDSC reviews developers, builders and their principals for related companies, insolvency proceedings, litigation, planning controversies and adverse media, including links to past investigations on the coast. Findings support investment and lending decisions and do not replace legal due diligence on title, planning compliance or licences by Spanish counsel.

faqs.q: Does TDSC work on matters involving Málaga TechPark companies?
faqs.a: Yes. TDSC researches technology companies, founders and investors connected to Málaga TechPark and the wider city cluster, covering corporate history, related entities, litigation and media in Spanish and English. This supports venture investments, acquisitions and commercial partnerships, and is scoped to the decision the client needs to make.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office or detectives in Málaga?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Málaga or elsewhere in Spain. Engagements are managed from Nashville. Where a matter needs local inquiries, TDSC coordinates private detectives holding the qualification required under Spanish law and works with the client's Spanish counsel under an agreed written scope.
